Read from `.design-foundations/copy/rule-coverage.json` and `generated/proof-summary.json` at assembly time, never typed. A **lint** is a check that runs over strings (`over`: **new** every New string, **kept** every kept string and every source string no row touches, **source** every string in the source, **examples** the guide's own examples, **code** the source code the checks read, **data** the revision data, **guide** this text); a **planted defect** is a string or an edit that breaks the rule, put into a throwaway copy by `prove-checks.mjs`, and the lint is proved only when the run reports it caught (189 unit proofs, 45 of them controls that must stay quiet, and 229 end-to-end proofs, 2 of them a control that must stay quiet, all behaving as planted). What no lint can see is checked by hand: the rows read, and the result.

| Rule | Lints that run over the strings | Planted defects | Checked by hand |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C1` Case | B1 (new), H17 (kept), H1 (source), H7 (code); the audit's own: C1-A, C1-B | 10 unit, 7 end to end | nothing a lint cannot see |
| `C2` Buttons | B1 (new), H12 (code), H8 (data); the audit's own: C2-A | 8 unit, 4 end to end | 11 rows read: 11 of 11 need the extra words: 3 name a provider (Sign in with Google, Sign up with Google), 2 are a count and its noun (Approve 3 events), 1 is the person's own voice (I've copied the secret), 1 is two actions in one button (Sign in and allow access), 4 carry a qualifier that separates the button from its neighbour (Ask Kiwi to check, Go to your classes, Create first MCP server, Assign existing MCP servers); none can lose a word without losing its object |
| `C3` Dates and times | B1 (new), H17 (kept), H1 (source), H2 (code), H20 (guide); the audit's own: C3-A | 12 unit, 6 end to end | nothing a lint cannot see |

| `C12` Empty states | B1 (new), H17 (kept), H1 (source); the audit's own: C12-A | 6 unit, 3 end to end | 74 rows read: read in full: 0 say "Nothing here" or "No … found"; each is a "No {things} yet" or "No {things} match" state line (C5's one-clause form, for a secondary pane), a sentence that names the first step, or a sentence that says who acts and when; 0 defects |
| `C13` Loading and progress | B1 (new), H17 (kept), H1 (source); the audit's own: C13-A, C13-B | 6 unit, 4 end to end | nothing a lint cannot see |
| `C14` Labels, helpers, placeholders | B1 (new), H17 (kept), H1 (source); the audit's own: C14-A, C14-B, C14-C | 14 unit, 6 end to end | 103 rows read: read in full, and each helper compared with the labels within 15 lines of its anchor by word overlap: 12 helper and label pairs overlap by 60% or more of the label's words (page descriptions that use the page title; a field's purpose beside its name), and in each the helper adds information beyond the label (a format, a default, a consequence or a purpose); 0 defects |

| `C16` Claims | B1 (new), H17 (kept), H1 (source), D12 (code), D12 (data), K11 (examples), D13 (data), D13 (guide); the audit's own: C16-A | 8 unit, 22 end to end | 36 rows read: 36 rows that state what the product does were checked against the code they run, and the ones that say who can act against the access model on `fix/access-control`: 5 were corrected (A-09.09 promised that deleting a webhook can't be undone, and A-09.42, the dialog's title and its button and the row's control said delete, when the backend only sets the webhook inactive: they now say deactivate; A-09.66's tooltip now says only what the page does: it shows the secret once; A-14.26 said everything Kiwi learned from it, where the code removes the comments, the summaries, the search index and the stored file; A-12.10 sent every non-admin to an administrator for what a class's instructor may do under the model); 31 hold, S-01.07 once the branch merges (it ships with or after it, like S-05.06) |
